description: Canonical operator control-loop board: reconcile/admission throughput, turn-submit dispatch, agent wrapper HTTP, webhooks, SCM writes, REST API, sweep/triage/backlog, merge and deploy, stage machine, and memory/lifecycle faults. Error-ratio and threshold panels mirror the exact PromQL of the matching rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml so the number on-call sees here equals the number that fired. Replaces operator-health.json, operator-workflows.json and tatara-operator.json (merged and deduped). The task-centric redesign (2026-07-12/13) repointed every panel querying a metric it deletes (operator_task_terminal_total's old phase/reason labels, tatara_cd_cascade_failed/stalled, tatara_cd_resolved_total, tatara_scan_*, tatara_issue_outcome_total, operator_writeback_outcome_total) onto the new Task stage machine, and deleted the writeback and systemic-grouping panels outright since those mechanisms are gone. scripts/check_metric_provenance.py now walks this file in CI, so a panel on a metric nobody emits fails the build instead of rendering empty forever. Repointed onto the tatara-operator v2.0.0 8-state Task lifecycle (2026-08-08, issue #97): operator_task_stage -> operator_task_state, operator_task_stage_age_seconds -> operator_task_state_age_seconds, and the stage/stageReason labels -> state / stateReason (terminal) / parkReason (park). Verified against the operator's internal/obs at origin/main and against live Prometheus, not assumed.

panels.title: Turn Submit (agent dispatch)

panels.description: Turn-submit throughput broken out by Task kind and result. result=ok is a successful dispatch, result=transient is a benign requeue (boot-race / 503 / 425 / 409 session-busy backpressure), result=error is a hard failure that backs off the reconcile. Fine-grained transport causes live on the Agent Wrapper HTTP row.
panels.title: Turn-submit rate by kind and result

panels.description: Fraction of turn submits that hard-errored over the last 15m, gated to >=10 submissions. Exact PromQL of the 'Operator turn submit failure ratio high' rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml (clamp_min avoids divide-by-zero on an idle operator). transient requeues are intentionally excluded.
panels.title: Turn-submit error ratio (alert: Operator turn submit failure ratio high)

panels.description: p95 wall-clock of SubmitTurn calls, broken out by Task kind. Red line at 30s mirrors the 'Operator turn submit p95 latency high' alert (which uses the aggregate p95 across all kinds).
panels.title: Turn-submit p95 duration by kind
Agent Wrapper HTTP

panels.description: Operator-to-wrapper HTTP call rate by method and outcome. outcome is ok, http_error (non-2xx response), transport_error (connection failure) or unreachable (no route to the pod).
panels.title: Agent HTTP rate by method and outcome

panels.description: Rate of transport-level agent HTTP failures (unreachable / timeout / transport_error) over 10m. Exact PromQL of the 'Operator agent HTTP failure spike' rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml.
panels.title: Agent HTTP transport errors (alert: Operator agent HTTP failure spike)

panels.description: p95 wall-clock of operator-to-wrapper HTTP calls by method.
panels.title: Agent HTTP p95 duration by method
Webhooks

panels.description: Inbound webhook event rate by provider and result. provider=github|gitlab; result includes ok, error, bad_signature, bad_request and the benign accepted/created/duplicate/ignored/reactivated/task_created outcomes.
panels.title: Webhook event rate by provider and result

panels.description: Fraction of webhook events that were error/bad_signature/bad_request over 15m. Exact PromQL of the 'Operator webhook error ratio high' rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml (clamp_min avoids idle divide-by-zero).
panels.title: Webhook error ratio (alert: Operator webhook error ratio high)

panels.description: p95 webhook handling wall-clock by provider. Slow apiserver/secret lookups surface here before GitHub's 10s delivery timeout.
panels.title: Webhook p95 handling duration by provider
SCM Writes

panels.description: SCM write operation rate by verb and result, filtered to kind=write (excludes read-only verbs like list_open_issues so the mix is not diluted by read traffic). result=ok succeeded, result=blocked was refused by an egress guard (benign), result=error is a genuine failure the error-ratio alert watches.
panels.title: SCM write rate by verb and result

panels.description: Fraction of SCM operations that errored over 15m. Exact PromQL of the 'Operator SCM write failure ratio high' rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml (clamp_min avoids idle divide-by-zero). Deliberately unfiltered by kind to match the alert's own aggregate.
panels.title: SCM error ratio (alert: Operator SCM write failure ratio high)

panels.description: SCM operations that errored, keyed by provider and classified HTTP status (or network for connect/timeout). Names WHICH status is driving the SCM error ratio.
panels.title: SCM request errors by provider and status
REST API

panels.description: Operator REST API request rate by handler endpoint and result.
panels.title: REST API request rate by endpoint and result

panels.description: p95 REST API handler execution wall-clock by endpoint.
panels.title: REST API p95 duration by endpoint
Reconcile & Task Throughput

panels.description: Reconcile throughput by CRD kind. result=ok|error|transient; this panel counts all outcomes.
panels.title: Reconcile rate by kind

panels.description: Aggregate reconcile error ratio (result=transient excluded, matching CONVENTIONS.md). Exact PromQL of the 'Operator reconcile error ratio high' rule in alerts/tatara-operator.yaml so the number here equals the number that paged.
panels.title: Reconcile error ratio (alert: Operator reconcile error ratio high)

panels.description: Tasks reaching a terminal state by state and kind. Under the v2.0.0 8-state lifecycle the terminal set is EXACTLY done|rejected: `failed` and `parked` are gone as states, because a failure now parks instead of terminating. The failure signal moved to operator_task_parked_total{parkReason} - see the 'Parks in the last hour by reason' panel and the 'Operator task failure spike' / 'Operator task park spike' alerts. This panel is the delivery-versus-rejection split only.
panels.title: Task terminal rate by state and kind

panels.description: Queued (not-yet-admitted) QueuedEvents per project and pool class. Leader-only gauge; max() collapses non-leader replicas. Red line at 10 mirrors the 'Operator queue depth backlog' alert (events backing up faster than they admit).
panels.title: Queue depth by project and class (alert: Operator queue depth backlog)

panels.description: Admitted in-flight QueuedEvents per project and pool class. Leader-only gauge; max() collapses non-leader replicas. Read alongside queue depth: high inflight + high depth means the lane is saturated (see the 'Operator tasks inflight pinned at cap' alert).
panels.title: Queue inflight by project and class

panels.description: Rate at which QueuedEvents are admitted into flight, split by pool class and Task kind. This is the throughput of the admission gate; a drop to zero while queue depth is non-zero means admission is stuck.
panels.title: Admission rate by class and kind

panels.description: Rate of admission declines by project, pool class and reason. reason=token_budget today. This is a 0-series until a project enables a token-budget window (issue #189); an empty panel means nothing has been declined in-window, not a broken query.
panels.title: Admission declines by reason (wired-but-quiet)
Sweep, Triage & Backlog

panels.description: Sweep runs that minted at least one Task, by project and target stage, over 15m (rate of operator_tasks_minted_per_sweep_count). Successor to tatara_scan_items_total, which the task-centric redesign deletes along with the old per-item scan-outcome breakdown (picked/skipped_dedup/skipped_cap/...) - the new sweep loop reports mint counts, not per-item outcomes.
panels.title: Sweep runs that minted a Task, by project and stage

panels.description: Rate of Tasks minted by the sweep loop, by project and target stage (rate of operator_tasks_minted_per_sweep_sum - the histogram's total-value series). Successor to tatara_scan_tasks_created_total, which the task-centric redesign deletes along with the by-kind breakdown; the new minted-Task metric is keyed by project and stage, not scan activity and kind.
panels.title: Tasks minted per sweep, by project and stage

panels.description: Seconds since each (project, activity) sweep last completed successfully (operator_sweep_last_success_timestamp_seconds). Grouped by project as well as activity: that gauge is written by every Project, so a max by (activity) alone reproduces the tatara-operator#441 clobber visually. A flat, climbing line is a sweep that has stopped running. The ALERT no longer reads this series - "Operator sweep heartbeat stale" reads time() - operator_sweep_next_expected_timestamp_seconds > 10800, which is cadence-aware; this panel is the human-readable freshness view. NOTE: contract K.1 declares no sweep-DURATION histogram, so the sweep's latency (as opposed to its liveness) is still not observable.
panels.title: Sweep freshness by project and activity (time since last success)

panels.description: Tasks currently sitting in state=new (the operator's own triage pass, 5m budget), by origin kind, plus parks with parkReason=triage-stalled over the last hour. v2.0.0 renamed the `triaging` stage to the `new` state. NOTE: state=new also holds every sweep-minted backlog owner, which is parked(backlog-sweep) and NEVER ages out by design (contract F.4's one deadline exemption), so a large steady population here is normal and only the triage-stalled park series shows triage failing to drain.
panels.title: Triage backlog and triage stalls

panels.description: Open bot-authored proposals per repo (leader-only gauge; max() collapses non-leader replicas). This is the standing backlog the brainstorm loop has generated and not yet had closed/declined. Watched against the project-wide maxOpenProposals cap.
panels.title: Open proposals by repo
Merge & Deploy (push-CD)

panels.description: Tasks currently in state=merged or state=deployed - the population of the push-CD pipeline. NAMING TRAP: under v2.0.0 these name the PHASE, not the milestone. `merged` means the verdict is approve and the operator owns the merge cursor, NOT that every MR is merged; per-MR truth stays on mr.status.state. They are the direct successors of the `merging` and `deploying` stages and carry the same F.4 budgets (merged 4h, deployed 2h). A sustained population past those budgets is the wedge signal; see the 'Tatara merge stage wedged' / 'Tatara deploy stage wedged' / 'Tatara delivery parked on a merge or deploy timeout' alerts in alerts/tatara-cd.yaml for the paging thresholds this panel visualizes.
panels.title: Tasks in merge/deploy state (push-CD pipeline population)

panels.description: Tasks currently in state=done. v2.0.0's `done` absorbed the old `delivered` stage, and a done Task is reaped at 48h (DeliveredRetention), so this gauge IS the rolling 48h delivery count - the deploy path's throughput signal. The blockage side of this path is the merge/deploy park reasons on the parks-by-reason panel and the merge/deploy alerts in alerts/tatara-cd.yaml.
panels.title: Delivered Tasks (rolling 48h population)
Memory & Lifecycle Faults

panels.description: Per-project tatara-memory stacks by phase. phase=Failed>0 is critical (agents for that project cannot read/write memory); see the 'Operator memory stack failed' alert.
panels.title: Memory stacks by phase (alert: Operator memory stack failed)

panels.description: Per-project memory-stack provisioning p95: time for a fresh project's memory stack to reach Ready. Gaps mean no provisioning happened in-window.
panels.title: Memory provision p95

panels.description: Agent-pod lifecycle fault rates: boot-crash (operator_agent_boot_crash_total{outcome=failed}), unreachable-termination (operator_agent_unreachable_termination_total), and orphan-reaped (operator_orphan_reaped_total). Backs the 'Operator agent boot crash budget exhausted' and 'Operator agent unreachable terminations' alerts. NOTE: boot_crash is wired-but-quiet - it reads 0 until a wrapper Pod exhausts the boot-respawn budget, so a flat zero line here is healthy.
panels.title: Agent lifecycle faults
State machine

panels.description: Current Task population per state (operator_task_state), stacked. This is the v2.0.0 8-state enum made visible: new, refined, under-implementation, awaiting-review, merged, deployed, done, rejected. Park is NOT a state any more - it is an orthogonal flag, so a parked Task still counts under whatever state it is in; see the 'Parks in the last hour by reason' panel for the park axis.
panels.title: Tasks per state

panels.description: How long each Task has sat in its current state (contract K.1's carry-adjusted operator_task_state_age_seconds), sorted worst-first. IMPORTANT: this gauge carries NO park dimension, so a legitimately parked Task (park is orthogonal to state in v2.0.0, and parked(backlog-sweep) never ages out at all) is indistinguishable here from a genuinely wedged one. Read a large age together with the parks-by-reason panel before calling it a wedge; the alert side is deliberately thresholded above ParkRetention (7d) for the same reason.
panels.title: State age by task (worst first)

panels.description: Parks in the last hour by parkReason (increase of operator_task_parked_total). Under v2.0.0 this is the ONLY counter of a failure: `failed` is gone as a state and a failure now parks. Unfiltered, so it includes the benign backlog-sweep and awaiting-human reasons the 'Operator task park spike' alert deliberately excludes - use that alert's filter as the read on what is actually a platform failure versus expected parking.
panels.title: Parks in the last hour by reason
